name: Peritoneal Mesothelioma In Situ
aliases: Mesothelioma in situ of the peritoneum

criteria.description: Presence of atypical mesothelial proliferation confined to the peritoneal surface without invasion
Loss of BAP1 expression in mesothelial cells confirmed by immunohistochemistry
Absence of radiologic evidence of invasive peritoneal mesothelioma or distant metastasis
Presence of unexplained persistent peritoneal symptoms or incidental detection during surgery

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of atypical mesothelial proliferation with BAP1 loss and no evidence of invasion or metastasis on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of invasive mesothelioma and other malignancies; molecular testing for BAP1 is critical.

pathognomonic.notes: Detected via imaging or during surgery

pathognomonic.symptomName: Loss of BAP1 protein expression in mesothelial cells
searchTerms: loss of BAP1 protein in lining cells
absent BAP1 expression in abdominal lining

common.symptomName: Abdominal distension due to minimal ascites
searchTerms: belly swelling from small fluid buildup
abdominal bloating due to minimal ascites
mild fluid in abdomen causing distension

common.notes: May be subtle in early stages

searchTerms: high blood levels of mesothelin peptides
mild anemia due to chronic illness
low red blood cells from long-term disease

rare.symptomName: Pleural effusion without evidence of pleural mesothelioma
rare.notes: May occur due to peritoneal-pleural communication
searchTerms: lung fluid buildup not from tumor

laboratory: Loss of BAP1 expression by immunohistochemistry
imaging: Localized peritoneal thickening without invasive masses on CT or MRI
genetic: BAP1 gene mutation or deletion in mesothelial cells
other: Histopathologic identification of atypical mesothelial proliferation confined to peritoneal surface

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of invasive tumor growth beyond mesothelial surface
Radiologic evidence of peritoneal masses and metastases
Positive immunohistochemical markers for carcinoma (e.g., PAX8)
Different molecular profile without BAP1 loss
Lack of cytologic atypia and BAP1 expression preserved
Associated with inflammatory or infectious peritoneal conditions

redFlags: Rapid progression to invasive peritoneal mesothelioma
Unexplained persistent abdominal distension with peritoneal thickening
Loss of BAP1 expression in mesothelial cells
references: Husain AN, Colby TV, Ordóñez NG, et al. Guidelines for pathologic diagnosis of malignant mesothelioma: 2017 update of the consensus statement from the International Mesothelioma Interest Group. Arch Pathol Lab Med. 2018;142(1):89-108.
Churg A, Galateau-Sallé F, Roggli V. Mesothelioma in situ: a proposal for diagnostic criteria. Mod Pathol. 2020;33(9):1773-1783.
